goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of five uncurated IMA-approved critical-element mineral species from the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 34, 35, 36, and 37), resolving four volume/page citation transcription typos from the Round 126 deferred queue.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Ginelfite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Jas Roux hydrothermal deposit, La Chapelle-en-Valgaudemar, Gap, Hautes-Alpes, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
type_specimens: Holotype 20023 (Museo di Storia Naturale of the Università di Pisa, Calci, Italy)
Holotype P1P 56/2022 (Department of Mineralogy and Petrology, National Museum, Prague, Czech Republic)

primary_source.citation: Biagioni C, Sejkora J, Moëlo Y, Favreau G, Bourgoin V, Boulliard J-C, Bonaccorsi E, Mauro D, Musetti S, Pasero M, Perchiazzi N, Ulmanová J (2025) Ginelfite, Ag2(Ag0.5Fe0.5)TlPb24.5(Sb,As)32.5S75.5, a new boxwork sulfosalt from Jas Roux, France: occurrence and crystal structure. European Journal of Mineralogy 37:319-335

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List (p. 82) lists the pre-refinement formula Ag2(Ag0.5Fe2+0.5)TlPb23.5(Sb,As)33.5S76, whereas the published primary description (Biagioni et al., 2025, pp. 319, 320, 323, 331) reports the end-member formula Ag2(Ag0.5Fe2+0.5)TlPb24.5(Sb,As)32.5S75.5 based on half-occupancy of the S(71) site and refined Pb/(Sb,As) site populations.

Table 2 (p. 322) prints the Ev(%) valence equilibrium error range (n = 35) as '-2.3–+1.7', whereas Section 4.1 prose (p. 323) misprints the upper bound sign as '-1.1 % (ranging between -2.3 % and -1.7 %)'.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Graulichite-(La)
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Patte d'Oie mine, Bou Skour Cu-hydrothermal mining district, Djebel Saghro mountain range, ~50 km southeast of Ouarzazate, Anti-Atlas, Morocco
type_specimens: Holotype 19924 (Museo di Storia Naturale, University of Pisa, Calci, Italy)

primary_source.citation: Biagioni C, Ciriotti ME, Favreau G, Mauro D, Zaccarini F (2022) Graulichite-(La), LaFe3+3(AsO4)2(OH)6, a new addition to the alunite supergroup from the Patte d'Oie mine, Bou Skour mining district, Morocco. European Journal of Mineralogy 34:365-374

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Table 1 (p. 369) prints the normalized oxide totals for both Domain #1 and Domain #2 as 100.00 wt%, whereas the arithmetic sums of the 13 rounded normalized oxide values are 100.02 wt% for both domains.

Because crystals of graulichite-(La) are porous and fragile (raw EPMA totals 78.34 wt% and 83.66 wt%, and only 47 unique reflections up to 2theta = 31.75 deg), the isotropic structure refinement with fixed Uiso (R1 = 0.0956) exhibits an apparent inversion of the tetrahedral X-O(1) (1.65(9) Å) vs X-O(2) (1.56(5) Å x 3) bond lengths that the authors explicitly note is a refinement artifact.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Karlseifertite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Second oxidation zone, Tsumeb mine, Tsumeb, Namibia (19°15' S, 17°42' E)
type_specimens: Holotype 76334 (Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, Los Angeles, California, USA)
Cotype 76335 (Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, Los Angeles, California, USA)

primary_source.citation: Kampf AR, Désor J, Ma C (2024) Karlseifertite, Pb(Ga2Ge)(AsO4)2(OH)6, a new dussertite-group mineral, from Tsumeb, Namibia. European Journal of Mineralogy 36:873-878

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 1 (p. 874) reports the mineral symbol as '(Warr symbol: Karl)', whereas the IMA-CNMNC Master List assigns Ksf.

Table 5 (p. 877) prints the mean bond lengths as <Pb-O> = 2.802 Å, <Ga-O> = 1.993 Å, and <As-O> = 1.694 Å, whereas the multiplicity-weighted arithmetic means of the listed bond distances (Pb-O2 2.785(7) x 6 and Pb-O3 2.838(4) x 6; Ga-O2 1.959(7) x 2 and Ga-O3 1.965(3) x 4; As-O1 1.671(13) x 1 and As-O2 1.699(7) x 3) are 2.812 Å, 1.963 Å, and 1.692 Å, respectively.

Table 6 (p. 877) prints the anion bond-valence sums for O1 and O2 as 1.81 and 1.95 v.u., whereas the rounded row contributions sum to 1.28 + 3 x 0.18 = 1.82 v.u. for O1 and 0.18 + 0.55 + 1.21 = 1.94 v.u. for O2.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Skogbyite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Långban Fe-Mn oxide deposit (59.86° N, 14.27° E), Filipstad Municipality, Värmland County, Bergslagen ore province, Sweden
type_specimens: Holotype GEO-NRM20230033 (Department of Geosciences, Swedish Museum of Natural History / Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, Stockholm, Sweden)

primary_source.citation: Jonsson E, Hålenius U, Majka J, Bosi F (2025) Skogbyite, Zr(Mg2Mn3+4)SiO12, a new zirconium mineral in the braunite group from Långban, Bergslagen, Sweden. European Journal of Mineralogy 37:269-277

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Table 1 (p. 271) prints the EPMA mean oxide total (19 point analyses) as 98.42 wt%, whereas the arithmetic sum of the 12 printed mean oxide values (ZrO2 14.24 + SiO2 10.51 + Al2O3 0.79 + La2O3 0.01 + Ce2O3 2.80 + Mn2O3 56.02 + Fe2O3 3.78 + CaO 0.06 + MgO 9.86 + ZnO 0.09 + PbO 0.04 + Na2O 0.01) is 98.21 wt%; additionally, the printed CaO mean (0.06 wt%) exceeds the printed CaO range (0.02–0.05 wt%).
In the empirical formula (pp. 269, 271, 273), the A/M(1) site population is written (Zr4+0.69Ce3+0.10Mg0.06Ca0.01Zn0.01Pb0.01)Σ0.87, whereas the rounded cation subscripts sum to 0.88 apfu.
Section 3 (p. 271) prints 'The c : a ratio calculated from the single-crystal unit-cell parameters is 0.4999', which is the inverted ratio a : c = 9.4914 / 18.9875 = 0.49988 (true c : a = 2.0005).
The Abstract (p. 269) states R1 = 0.0460 for 648 unique reflections with I > 2sigma(I), whereas Section 6.2 (p. 273) and Table 3 (p. 274) report 658 unique reflections with I > 2sigma(I).

Table 6 (p. 275) prints the BVS of M(3) and M(4) as 2.34 and 2.43 v.u., whereas the rounded bond-valence contributions sum to 2 x (0.54 + 0.41 + 0.21) = 2.32 v.u. and 2 x (0.46 + 0.57 + 0.19) = 2.44 v.u., respectively.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Tetrahedrite-(Cd)
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: 7th and 8th levels of the S-1 vein, Radětice shaft (49°38'20.44" N, 14°05'13.66" E), ~300 m east of Radětice, 5 km southeast of Příbram, central Bohemia, Czech Republic
type_specimens: Holotype P1P 43/2022 (Department of Mineralogy and Petrology, National Museum in Prague, Czech Republic; polished section)
Holotype fragment 20025 (Museo di Storia Naturale of the Università di Pisa, Calci, Italy; grain used for single-crystal X-ray diffraction)

primary_source.citation: Sejkora J, Biagioni C, Škácha P, Musetti S, Kasatkin AV, Nestola F (2023) Tetrahedrite-(Cd), Cu6(Cu4Cd2)Sb4S13, from Radětice near Příbram, Czech Republic: the new Cd member of the tetrahedrite group. European Journal of Mineralogy 35:897-907

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 897) misprints the mineral name as 'Tennantite-(Cd) is cubic, I-43m, with unit-cell parameters a = 10.504(3) Å, V = 1158.9(9) Å3, and Z = 2' when reporting the unit-cell parameters of holotype tetrahedrite-(Cd).
Table 3 (p. 901) prints the calculated d-spacing for reflection 4 4 4 (Icalc = 3) without a decimal point as '1516' instead of '1.516' Å.
Table 6 (p. 903) lists X(3)–S(1) x 3 = 2.435(3) Å, whereas Section 5.2 prose (p. 903) writes 'The X(3) site has an average bond distance of 2.434 Å (Table 6)'.
